Supporting Document Supporting Document c) REVENUE REPORT. Supporting Document d) Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held December 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 15.94 acres of land located southwest of the intersection of US Highway 30 and Christensen Road. e) Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held December 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, to receive comments and input for the Ridge Urban Renewal Plan and Project as required by Wyoming Statute §15-9-109. f) Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held December 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, to receive comments regarding the proposed conveyance of certain City-owned real property to Cheyenne LEADS for economic development and stormwater management purposes, as required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-112(b).

28. ADJOURN.

flags.msg: This item is designated for the consent agenda, meaning it is enacted by a single motion with no separate discussion unless a governing-body member pulls it (with two supporting members). Substantive policy can pass with essentially zero deliberation — request removal from consent if you want it discussed.

The proposed substitute removes one section from the site plan applicability section in the that was proposed to be added by the Planning Commission. That section in the applicability section of the site plan says that existing nonconforming agricultural uses are exempt from site plan, which is actually generally true of all existing uses. They're all exempt from site plans. And we take the intent of that language and put it into the nonconformances section, which is where we talk about grandfathered uses. And we add language to that section in every subsection of the nonconforming uses section to clarify that nonconforming buildings are allowed to continue if they're annexed to the city, nonconforming uses are allowed to continue when they're annexed to the city, and nonconforming site conditions are allowed to continue when annexed to the city. Right now, the Unified Development Code only says uses that were approved prior to the adoption of the UDC receive nonconforming status. So if a property in the county was developed post 2012 met all county requirements, they could be nonconforming when they are annexed into the city. And so this section would allow those annexed properties to continue as nonconforming once they're annexed to the city, if they were legally established in the county.

turns.text: To 149,800. This contract modification will result in no additional financial commitment from the city of Cheyenne or the US endowment. The funding has been reallocated among budget categories and will not impact the awarded grant Um, this request is a result of an approved budget modification between the city of Cheyenne and the US endowment for forestry and communities innovative finance for national forest grant number The city of Cheyenne was awarded 250,000 in 2024 to pilot the potential use of the Wyoming clean water revolve state revolving loan fund program to fund wildfire risk reduction activities with the town of encampment. Representatives from the Board of Public Utilities, the city of Cheyenne, the town of encampment, the National Forest Foundation, and World Resources Institute have utilized the US endowment funding to develop the fuels reduction project and apply for the clean water state revolving loan fund program. The loan application was successful. The total amount loan amount awarded was $1 with a maximum 75% principal loan forgiveness. National Forest Foundation is going to be covering the remaining 25% of the principal and the loan origination fee. This contract modification will ensure that the National Forest Foundation is able to continue to provide management to the project and this will serve as a model for other communities looking for innovative funding opportunities to reduce wildfire risk. docs.title: RESOLUTION – Opposing federal legislation or regulations that increase maximum truck size or weight limits on National Highways. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)
docs.bodySnippet: [p1] RESOLUTION NO. __________ ENTITLED: "A RESOLUTION OPPOSING FEDERAL LEGISLATION OR REGULATIONS THAT INCREASE MAXIMUM TRUCK SIZE OR WEIGHT LIMITS ON NATIONAL HIGHWAYS." WHEREAS, the City of Cheyenne recognizes the critical role that freight transportation plays in supporting Wyoming's economy, interstate commerce, and the movement of goods throughout the United States; WHEREAS, the City of Cheyenne is committed to maintaining a safe, efficient, and fiscally responsible transportation system for residents, businesses, visitors, emergency responders, and the goods movement industry alike; WHEREAS, proposals have been introduced in Congress from time to time to increase the allowable weight or size of commercial motor vehicles operating on the National Highway System, including proposals to increase the federal gross vehicle weight limit fro m 80,000 pounds to 91,000 pounds; WHEREAS, heavier commercial vehicles would place additional stress on roads, bridges, intersections, and other transportation infrastructure that was not originally designed for substantially greater vehicle weights; WHEREAS, local governments are responsible for maintaining significant portions of the transportation network used daily by commercial trucks, and increased infrastructure deterioration resulting from heavier trucks would create additional maintenance and replacement costs without a dedicated federal funding source; WHEREAS, commercial trucks travel billions of miles annually on local roads, and communities such as Cheyenne experience substantial truck traffic that is vital to commerce but also contributes to ongoing infrastructure maintenance needs; WHEREAS, winter weather conditions, wind -gusts, steep grades, and periodic traffic congestion in and around Cheyenne already create operational and public safety challenges involving commercial vehicles; WHEREAS, the U.S. Department of Transportation has previously reported higher crash involvement rates for trucks weighing between 91,000 and 97,000 pounds compared to today's federally permitted 80,000-pound trucks, and has found that longer combination ve hicles require greater stopping distances and experience higher out-of-service violation rates; WHEREAS, the City of Cheyenne believes any proposal to increase truck size or weight should fully account for its impacts on public safety, local infrastructure, and taxpayer costs before being considered by Congress; and [p2] WHEREAS, protecting the safety of Cheyenne residents, preserving public infrastructure, and avoiding unfunded federal mandates are fundamental responsibilities of the City. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, that the City of Cheyenne formally opposes federal legislation or administrative action that would increase the allowable size or weight of commercial motor vehicles operating on the National Highway System unless and until it can be demonstrated that such increases will not adversely impact public safety, local infrastructure, or impose additional unfunded costs on state and local governments; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the City encourages Congress to preserve existing federal truck si

Date: September 14, 2026 ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ Background: This resolution formally adopts "Prospering Together: Laramie County’s Path to a Sustainable Future" as the City of Cheyenne’s Comprehensive Climate Action Plan (CCAP) pursuant to the $1,000,000 EPA Climate Pollution Reduction Grant accepted under Resolution No. 6388 which was adopted on February 26, 2024. This plan was developed in partnership with Lotus Engineering & Sustainability, LLC , and was previously managed by the City’s prior Economic Resource Administrator. While the plan serves as a foundational policy guide, its adoption does not commit the City to any individual measure, leaving specific future implementation actions to be evaluated separately. Adoption of this plan gives the City a leg up on future funding opportunities for eligible projects related to reducing emissions and improving community resilience such as community solar, energy efficiency retrofits for municipal facilities, fleet electrification, active transportation infrastructure, and sustainable waste management initiatives. This is needed to fulfil Wyoming State Statute 15-1-506 and allow the Future Land Use Map Amendment to be considered by the Governing Body. The Planning Commission heard a future land use map amendment at their September 8, 2026, meeting and unanimously voted 6-0 to deny the amendment. Wyoming State Stature requires a majority of the Commission to vote in favor which would require four members to have voted ‘yes’ on a motion to approve. Wyoming State Statute allows the Governing Body to overrule the Planning Commission and consider plans or plan amendments the Planning Commission disapproves. PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT 2101 O’Neil Avenue Cheyenne, WY 82001 (307) 637-6282 cheyennecity.org MEMO To: Honorable Mayor Patrick Collins and Members of the City Council From: Charles W. Bloom Subject: CheyenneNext - Comprehensive Plan Update Date: August 24, 2026 ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Background: The item for consideration is a contract for professional services to update the Community Character element of the Cheyenne Comprehensive Plan (PlanCheyenne). The Governing Body approval schedule is as follows: • Introduction and Referral August 24, 2026 • Finance Committee September 9, 2026 (Wednesday) • Final Consideration September 14, 2026 Eleven firms responded to the Request for Proposals (RFP). Three submittals were disqualified for failing to meet submittal requirements. The remaining eight submittals were evaluated by a selection committee comprising representatives from the City Council, Planning and Development, Engineering, the MPO, Laramie County Planning and Development, the Planning Commission, and a local developer. The committee shortlisted and conducted in-person interviews with four firms: • Cushing Terrell • Houseal Lavigne Associates LLC • Kimley-Horn • Logan Simpson Design Inc. Additional submittals evaluated but not shortlisted included Design Workshop, Glenn A. Rick Engineering & Development Company, Lotus Engineering and Sustainability, LLC, and Orion Planning + Design. Following competitive evaluations and in-person firm presentations, Houseal Lavigne ranked highest among the competing consultants. None of the submitting firms qualified for local preference. Through contract negotiations, staff worked with Houseal Lavigne to optimize both the schedule and fee. The scope was refined to condense the project timeline from 18 months down to 14 months (targeting final adoption in November 2027) while incorporating land-use scenario planning and Placer.ai mobile device data to analyze regional commuting patterns. The resulting professional services agreement is for a not-to-exceed amount of $351,790. [p2] Project Scope & Deliverables Project timing and milestones are detailed in Exhibit A of the contract. Robust Steering Committee and public engagement will drive the process throughout. The final deliverable will be a clear, concise, easy-to-read Comprehensive Plan designed to guide Cheyenne’s future growth under current and projected development conditions. The plan will feature user-friendly goals and actionable statements to evaluate local development regulations and guide future land-use and policy decisions. Supporting deliverables include clear graphics, an implementation framework, and key maps covering future land use, active transportation networks, development barriers, and residential and technology growth suitability. Funding Sources The total contract price has been negotiated to be $351,790.00 with a completion date of in November of 2027. TJ Barttelbort, Purchasing Manager City of Cheyenne, Wyoming (307) 773-1045 Published in: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle Dates: September 11, 18, 2026 [p4] January 28, 2026 To Whom It May Concern: This letter confirms that LN Curtis & Sons, Inc is the sole authorized distributor of Globe turnout gear and boots for the Municipal Fire Service Market for the State of Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. By way of background, in the fire service / first responder markets, MSA imposes specific requirements upon our distributors, which can result in a small number of distributors authorized to call upon a particular region. items.title: CALL MEETING TO ORDER.
CALL ROLL.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE.

CONSENT AGENDA. (All agenda items listed with the designation of are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON AUGUST 10, 2026.
PUBLIC HEARINGS:

Transfer of location and ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Capital City Hospitality, LLC d/b/a Wyoming Discount Liquor, 3501 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by 1734 Partners, LLC, 1734 Meadowland Dr., Cheyenne, WY).
RESOLUTION – Naming a triangle-shaped parcel of real property located at the intersection of Randall Avenue and Cribbon Avenue as the ‘Dr. Robert M. Farr Park.’ (SPONSORS – DR. ALDRICH AND MR. WHITE)
RESOLUTION – Opposing federal legislation or regulations that increase maximum truck size or weight limits on National Highways.(SPONSOR – DR. ALDRICH)
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:

Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Police Department, and Laramie County School District Number One for the School Resource Officers Program. (Revenue to the City) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)

Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Ardurra Group, Inc. for Operation Modification at the Pershing, Converse, and 19th Street Roundabout. (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
Right-of-Way Use Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and CSRE Properties Wyoming, LLC for two connections of storm sewer pipe from detention ponds in the Ventura Drive right-of-way.
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives and Laramie County to provide services to the Laramie County Juvenile Crisis Shelter. (Revenue to the City)

Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives and Laramie County to provide probation/diversion services to youth appearing in both the Laramie County Circuit Court and the Municipal Court. (Revenue to the City)
Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Houseal Lavigne Associates, LLC for the Cheyenne-Next Comprehensive Plan update. (One Time State Distribution Funds and General Fund)
Grant Award Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security for the Fiscal Year 2025 State Homeland Security Program. (Homeland Security grant)
CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:

Contract Modification #1 to Contract #8374 between the City of Cheyenne and the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027. (General Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS/PURCHASES/REQUESTS FOR PROPOSALS:

Consideration of Bid #S-22-26 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Legacy Construction Group for the Christensen Road Detention Erosion Mitigation project. (2012 & 2017 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE) (POSTPONED FROM AUGUST 10, 2026)
Consideration of Bid #S-1-27 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and STC Construction Co., Inc. for the Cahill and Lions Park Pavement Restoration project. (General Fund)

Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Motorola Solutions / Absolute Solutions, Inc. for the purchase of Motorola portable, mobile, and base station radios for the Animal Control Division. (General Fund Reserves)

Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Motorola Solutions / Bearcom for the purchase of Motorola mobile radios for the Cheyenne Police Department. (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund)
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
VOUCHER REPORT.
REVENUE REPORT.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held September 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 162.42 acres of land located west of South Greeley Highway, south of West College Drive, and southwest of and adjacent to the intersection of Apple Street and York Avenue.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held September 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 652.67 acres of land located south of Interstate 80, southeast of Otto Road, and west of Interstate 25.

Announcement that a Calcutta benefitting Children’s Western Wish Foundation will be held on Sunday, September 27, 2026 at 3:00 p.m., at Frontier Park, Cheyenne, Wyoming, in conjunction with the 2026 Indian Relay Championship of Champions (10% of proceeds go to bona fide charity).

Announcement that due to City offices being closed for the Labor Day holiday on Monday, September 7, 2026, regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference meeting as follows: Public Services Committee will meet Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at Noon and Finance Committee will meet Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at Noon.

Announcement that the following ordinances that were postponed in April 2026 will return to the Public Services Committee on Tuesday, September 8, 2026 for consideration: ORDINANCE - 2nd READING - Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road. ORDINANCE - 2nd READING - Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classification of AG - Agricultural and P - Public for land annexed to the City of Cheyenne located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road. ORDINANCE - 2nd READING - Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located west of Roundtop Road and adjacent to Happy Jack Road from AG - Agricultural to BP - Business Park.
OTHER BUSINESS:
ADJOURN.

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk August 10, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel (arriving at 6:02), Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda ). Dr. Rinne declared a conflict of interest related to agenda item #8(b) and vacated Council Chambers . Upon request by Mr. Moody, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Laybourn and Mr. White, item #10(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present in Council Chambers . Following announcement of the vote, Dr. Rinne returned to Council Chambers. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on Ju ly 27, 2026. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Aldrich moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comments were made by: Heather Madrid, Brian Pixley and Charles Miller. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins and Dr. Emmons. (#4691) ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classification of BP – Business Park for land annexed to the City of Cheyenne, located west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by M r. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comments were made by: Heather Madrid and Charles Miller. docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk July 13, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn (arriving at 6:02), Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave, Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Proclamation recognizing members of the Cheyenne Laramie County America 250 Commission. Mayor Collins read the proclamation into the record and expressed appreciation to members of the Commission. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mayor Collins, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, items #22 and #26(b) were removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items , seconded by Dr. Aldrich. M otion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on June 22, 2026. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Cheyenne Railyard LLC d/b/a The Railyard – Cheyenne, 115 W. 15th St., Cheyenne, WY. There being no comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15- 1-402 exist for about 34.46 acres of land located west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road. Public comments were made by: Brad Emmons, AVI, P.C., Agent for the applicant , David Kniseley, Heather Madrid, Kay McAdams, Jim Chiro, Donna D undon, Charles Miller, Brian Pixley, Janet Tolman and Thomas White . Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. Well so obviously this means something to me and I think it should mean something to the entire city one of the great things about growing up in Cheyenne for me was that a lot of things happened here and over the 50 years that I think about I've been connected to the city in some sort of way I'm proud of the fact that this is a city that has had guts and insight and to do something different to try something that wasn't happening everywhere else as you know that this court the juvenile court was something that was established in this city and literally almost 50 years ago um I started in 1971 working as a probation officer for that court and it's been going on since then I'm proud of that fact because this city seemed to know and have the insight to create a program to create a court that not only was best practice driven but it was best practice driven before we knew what best practice was it was doing things that they're doing now on a regular basis throughout the country and it's doing those things because it's been proven by research it's been proven by experts that in the field that the kind of things we were doing in little old Cheyenne are the kind of things they Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins (via Zoom joining at 7:11 p.m. and leaving at 9:18 p.m.) COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom joining at 6:06 p.m.), Tom Segrave, Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Reappointments of Deputy Sheriff Timothy Johnson, Lieutenant Joel Hickerson, Kathy Emmons, Jeffrey O’Holleran and Mike Beitz to the Laramie County Community Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board; Anthony Ortiz to the Tourism Promotion Joint Powers Board; Andi Mikkelson, Richard Vallee, Michael Rucker and JC Manalo to the Transit Advisory Board; Katye Ames to the Urban Renewal Authority Board and Jasper James “JJ” Chen to the Cheyenne/Laramie County Economic Development Joint Powers Board.

Appointments of Michael Sanchez to the Laramie County Community Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board; Bria Hammock and Barbara Sandick to the Downtown Development Authority and Josie Malloy to the Tourism Promotion Joint Powers Board.
VOUCHER REPORT.
REVENUE REPORT.

Announcement that a calcutta benefitting Cheyenne area charities will be held on Saturday, July 25, 2026 at 5:30 p.m. in the Cowboy Bistro, located beside the Rodeo Committee Cabin at Frontier Park, Cheyenne, Wyoming, in conjunction with the 2026 Cheyenne Frontier Days Rodeo (10% of proceeds go to bona fide charities).

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held July 13, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Cheyenne Railyard LLC d/b/a The Railyard – Cheyenne, 115 W. 15th St., Cheyenne, WY.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held July 13, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 34.46 acres of land located west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road.
OTHER BUSINESS:
ADJOURN.

docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee - 06-02-26] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee - 06-02-26 Context/Agenda: good afternoon everybody it's high noon in old Cheyenne welcome to the June 2nd Finance Committee meeting like call that meeting to order ask everybody in the public here to make sure your phones are on vibrate or mute but making public comment clearly identifies yourself use the raised hand function online and our staff will let you know you can unmute yourself uh after the completion of this agenda no additional business will be discussed all uh communications go through the chair and with that clerk read the first item number nine ordinance third reading amending and updating the solid waste fee schedule in accordance with section 8.44.010 010 of the m municipal code of the city of Cheyenne Wyoming and repealing ordinance number 4621 staff report good afternoon craig Levoy public works um the WDQ requires municipalities to update our integrated solid waste master plan every 10 years and we did a full cost analysis with this in 2019 and these are the rates that they proposed for the next 10 years and the increases will be for residential trash and recycling 1% commercial trash they'll be 3% commercial recycling will be at 5% disposable at our transfer station is 2% and rolloffs are 3% and our yard waste services will increase by 1% and I recommend approval thank you any questions from anyone in the committee for staff seeing none we'll go to public comment in the room no public comment in the room public comment online no public comment online close public comment come back to the committee any final questions or comments okay what's your pleasure mr chair I move to approve on third and final reading moved by Councilman White second by Councilman Wolfe any further comments all those in favor signify by saying "Aye." Any opposed? no that motion is uh to the governing body will be to approve at the next meeting with Councilman Moody voting no next item number 13 ordinance third reading approving and establishing revised water and sewer rates tap and system development fees administrative fees service charges and penalties and septic and commercial waste stump rates as recommended by the board of public utilities staff report mr chairman and committee Brad Bowen admin manager for Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities in front of you is the annual rate ordinance for rates to be effective October 1 a quick summary of the rates would be a 3% in the monthly service fee a 5% in tier one and tier 2 rates on the residential side commercial side is going to be based pretty much by a percentage of overall usage system development fees at 5% administrative fees were modified based off of covering costs and septic and commercial dump rates increased by 5% and I stand for any questions questions or comments from the committee for staff let's see and none we'll go to public comment in the room any public comment online back to the committee can I get a motion uh Mr chairman um I move to approve on third and final reading second moved by Councilman Wolfe second by Councilman White any further discussion all in favor signify by saying

Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (arriving at 6:01 p.m.), Tom Segrave, Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Expression of A ppreciation of the 2025- 2026 Mayor’s Youth Council and S tate of the Youth Address was made. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item #19 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. W olfe, item #28(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. White moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Dr. Emmons moved to postpone to June 8, 2026, seconded by Mr. Segrave. [CA] Application for a microbrewery permit application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Jagerhund Brewing, LLC d/b/a Jagerhund Brewing, 3521 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.

Urban Renewal Authority 2025 Annual Report. Mr. Segrave moved to acknowledge receipt of the report, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich.

All opposed All right with that the motion passes Um and then with that we'll turn it over for um the first order business Item A request PUDC-26-66 conditional use request for outdoor sales within the LI zone located at lot 2 block 1 Overland Trails Business Park The agent is Jennifer Elram and case planners Morgan Dennis Thank you Please please go ahead Chair members of the board Morgan Dennis Planning and Development This is a conditional use request for outdoor storage and sales at lot 2 block one Overland Trails Business Park This parcel is located in the LI Light Industrial Zone District with surrounding zones being LI and CB Community Business The future land use map designates this area as mixeduse employment This designation promotes the development of industrial and commercial uses The proposed use is an expansion of the use on the property to the south The property to the south is currently being used for outdoor sales per the code The applicant initially asked for outdoor storage but with this being an expansion of an existing sta site staff added outdoor sales to the approved motion to reduce the possibility of the applicant needing to return before the board for changes during the site plan process The site is currently vacant but there is a site plan submitted with this conditional use This site will likely have to go through the site plan process and meet the standards for the light industrial zone district The operating characteristics will be complimentary to the surrounding area Business hour hours and number of trips are expected to be no different than those of the existing business There are no expected visible or audible impacts to the property The intent of the LI zone is for uses that cannot readily be fit into other general business or mixeduse areas due to nature or intensity of operations Outdoor storage and sales is within the intent of the LI zone as it is a component of this business that is not compatible with other commercially zoned areas With this staff recommends approval and I stand for questions Thank you Any questions for staff thank you Is there anyone from the applicant that would like to speak tonight thank you All right Any other public testimony all right With that we'll close public comment and the uh any any comment from anyone on the board All right The chair will maintain a motion Mr Chairman I move to approve a conditional use request for the use of outdoor sales and outdoor storage at lot 2 block 1 Overland Trails Business Park as presented by the applicant as the application meets all review

docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee 05-19-26] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee 05-19-26 Context/Agenda: okay it's high noon in Old Cheyenne welcome to the May 19th 2026 meeting of the Finance Committee of the governing body I'd like to call that meeting to order and if you're in the room make sure all your electronic devices are on silent or vibrate uh when making comments online use the raised hand function and all communications go through the chair and with that clerk first item number 6A application for a micro brewery permit filed with the city clerk's office for Joerger Hun Brewing LLC doing business as Joerger Hun Brewing 3521 East Lincolnway Cheyenne Wyoming staff report mr chairman members of the committee Kylie Soden city clerk the item before you is an application for a micro brewery permit submitted by Jagger Hun Brewing LLC doing business as Jagger Hun Brewing to be located at 3521 East Lincolnway the application has been reviewed by applicable city departments and the Wyoming Liquor Division and the requirements for the application have been met I am happy to answer any questions you may have any comments or questions from the committee for Madame Clerk no okay we'll go to public comment yes sir uh hello I am Fred Hirs owner of Yer Hun you have any questions for me any questions for the applicant you're off easy today okay any other public comment in the room any public comment online seeing no public comment we'll come back to the committee what's your pleasure uh Mr chairman I move to approve it's been moved by Councilman Moody seconded by Councilman Wolfe any further comments all in favor signify by saying "Aye." Aye. seeing there's none opposed that vote is unanimous the recommendation of the Finance Committee at the next meeting of the governing body will be to approve next item number 10 ordinance third reading amending enforcement and permitting requirements related to oversized vehicles and making conforming amendments staff report welcome Dr aldrich good afternoon um Dr michelle Aldrich City Council Ward Three um just uh bringing this uh ordinance amendment back um before the committee today again um there is a substitute that u Mr hopinson I believe is going to address but the uh primary focus of this ordinance is to uh limit the number of permits that individuals may apply for from the police department uh to two for um an u an ability to have their oversized vehicles u parked um on the street in order to load and unload those vehicles and um also just a reminder that it would also uh move this from being having to be complaint driven um to where a a police officer who would is driving by would be able to uh enforce this uh rather than having it only be complaint driven so those are the two primary changes um for this and I um would if you have any questions I'm sure that um Chief Francisco um or Chief Dyron uh would be able to answer those regarding safety of um large fire trucks and things like that around these vehicles um the difference that this has made over the last nine months that we've had this in place uh just a reminder this ordinance runs 5 days before Memorial Day which will be coming

would change that and make enforcement of the oversized vehicles exclusively in CPD's province So it take removes it from the compliance department removes it as a nuisance in the city code It changes docs.title: Word-for-word transcript — Work Session - City Employee Wage Structure - 05-01-26
docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Work Session - City Employee Wage Structure - 05-01-26] Context/Agenda: # Work Session - City Employee Wage Structure - 05-01-26 Context/Agenda: uh Councilman Cray we just have uh Councilman White and Dr. Emmons online good afternoon and thank you for being here uh to the May 1st uh city county work or city county city work session uh today uh the mayor and staff are going to talk to us about a city employee wage structure um I don't know how would you gentlemen like to handle this would you like us to hold questions until you're done or ask um totally up to you Mr president any I ask the questions when you when they come up we'll do our best to answer them all right if we have I don't know about you guys as I get older I forget things when I wait till the end and so I would uh just bring them to us could be an advantage though for Oh let me rethink that okay if we have questions we'll ask them as we go and we do have uh two council folks uh Dr. Emmons and Councilman White online joining us today as well with that Mr mayor take it away um President Crave members of the City Council for the record I'm Mayor Patrick Collins you know I appreciate the opportunity to talk about our city employees and our efforts to make the city of Cheyenne an employer of choice by making sure our employees are properly compensated I want to thank our chief of staff Amber Ash for putting together this presentation uh it's a very pretty presentation and and her touch is very evident with that uh and director Hos for uh his comments and for leading the effort to recruit and retain our talented workforce today the city has 394 non-uniformed full-time employees and 310 part-time employees serving the residents of the city of Cheyenne we do a compensation study every two years and what we've learned that after each study we were required to do a large salary adjustment to bring our employees back into compensation or their compensation back into their proper pay grade a couple of years ago we looked into this challenge of how we move our employees through their paygrades from the time they're hired to the end of their careers and we adopted a step program that we use in a couple of ways we use it one to calculate the beginning wage we offer prospective new employees it recognizes their past work experience and slots them into the proper place in the pay grade it also helps reduce compression by ensuring their pay progresses with experience today um the system uh that we use uh annually gives our employees 135th of their pay grade in a wage adjustment to keep their salary at the proper place in their pay grade pay grade as they move through their career with the city we chose that 35-year step uh increment and honestly it was uh maybe a best guess as a place to start to meet the goal of keeping our employees in the right place in their pay grades we've learned that that 35 steps is too long and the increment is too small to effectively keep our employees in the proper place our analysis shows that the proper increment should be figured over 25 years that means an employee receive 125th of their pay grade as a salary adjustment annually

docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee - 04-21-26 1] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee - 04-21-26 Context/Agenda: hi noon in old Cheyenne I'd like to call the April 21st meeting of the Finance Committee to order if you're in the room please be sure your cell phones are on vibrator turned off when making public comment clearly identify yourself making public comment online use the raised hand function uh in person turn on the microphone and at the end of the agenda there will be no additional business discussed and as always all communications go through the chair with that clerk first item number 15 ordinance third reading appropriating money for the Reed Avenue corridor project staff report no staff report well we're pretty aware of what it is so uh we'll go to public comment any public comment in the room good afternoon Sophia May Cheyenne DDA executive director um the as I noted last session last Finance Committee um actually apologize I wasn't here um the during council meeting uh the Cheyenne DDA supports this appropriation of the 5 million for the read rail corridor uh we believe that although the scope has changed significantly since the uh feasibility study that was produced the plan the design that's moving forward is more like an urban greenway and we believe that that connectivity that utilization of the space um throughout the summer months in downtown Cheyenne as well as providing an opportunity for the reinvestment into the historical area of downtown is really critical and um we support this And please let me know if you have any questions any comments or questions from the committee to our DDA director any public comment online seeing none can I get a motion mr chairman um I move to uh approve uh on third and final reading second it's been moved by Councilman Wolfe second by Councilman White any further discussion all in favor signify by saying "Aye." Aye. oppose no the recommendation of the Finance Committee at the next meeting of the governing body will be to approve next item number 23 resolution approving a proposition to impose the 1% specific purpose sales and use tax in Larmy County state of Wyoming for the exclusive purpose of funding specific purposes for spec for specific amounts the propositions to be voted on at the election to be held on August 18th of 2026 staff report Norman um through you to the committee um before you is a proposition um outlining all of the ballot items um across the county um for consideration and approval this will be identical across all governing bodies um and this will be what will go before the voters for approval and I'm happy to answer any questions any comments or questions from the committee to the chief of staff uh Mr chairman Councilman Wolfe uh thank you Mr chairman through you um Madam Chief of Staff I just want to express my appreciation to you and to the mayor and um to all the people that you worked so hard with um on this is such an important matter uh for the community Cheyenne for the county and for the small towns and uh your efforts and the mayor's efforts and your staff are very much appreciated thank you thank you councilman Moody thank you Mr chairman

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk March 23, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date beginning at 7:38 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. Absent: Mr. Esquibel. Also present: Luisa Walsh, Deputy City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Mayor Collins provided opening remarks regarding ongoing collective labor bargaining and acknowledged the concerns brought forth regarding salaries. He referenced a spreadsheet comparing the salaries of Local #279 to other departments throughout Wyoming and Colorado and emphasized we are comparable with other departments noting Cheyenne firefighters are offered reimbursement for education, whereas other departments do not offer this. Mayor Collins reviewed the City’s current compensation offer which includes maintaining the 3% COLA increase that was instituted in January, a 3% increase in base wage s, an additional 3.5% increase to Captain and 4.75% to Battalion Chief to address compression, adjust probationary firefighter step to 5% less than firefighter step 4 and increase medical, longevity and specialty pay by 3%. Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, requested a recess to review the proposal at 7:45 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the HR conference room to caucus. Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 8:20 p.m. Mr. Thoms thanked the Mayor and City Council for their part in moving towards resolution. He stated that the Union was willing to move forward with the following framework: a ccept the 3% base pay increase with the understanding that it is a market base adjustment and not a COLA, an extension of the COLA sunset clause on page 34, Section 21 of the current Collective Labor Agreement to extend through the new ly proposed agreement, and request City acceptance of the MERP (Medical Expense Reimbursement Plan) language as proposed by the Union. Mayor Collins reviewed the Vacation proposed language in Section 26 and advised that if the City and the Union can agree to the proposal, he would consider the MERP proposal. Mr. Thoms proposed amending the language to allow the four slots to be designated as either vacation or E.O.D. slots. Following discussion with Deputy Chief Rodgers, Mayor Collins confirmed mutual understanding of the vacation language, and both parties a greed to the revised terms including MERP language . Regarding the MERP, Mayor Collins indicated general agreement, with the exception that the City would not be required to contribute for firefighters not actively working or contributing. 03-20-26 Context/Agenda: hello and welcome to the March 20th uh City Council work session Today we're going to hear from the downtown development authority As is typical with these meetings there will be no questions from the public Uh I did talk with Sophia ahead of time and she says it's okay if we want to ask questions as we progress through the the meeting So if you have questions uh please address them to her Um with that said uh Sophia kick it off and tell us what's going on Thank you All right Good afternoon everyone My name is Sophia Maize I'm the executive director of the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority and I'm here today to um talk about that Um I want to open by first addressing the um the elephant in the room uh that there's a a narrative in the community that you've probably heard about the DDA lately that we don't do anything We're ineffective We don't know what's going on That downtown is struggling and we're not helping that it's a conflict of us a conflict of interest for us to be tied to the city and that maybe even we shouldn't exist at all When I joined the DDA last March I found an organization that was struggling to find its footing compliance gaps a new plan of development but not a very um not a very good organizational strategy and a community that had lost confidence in us Today I'm going to show you exactly what we've been working on for the past year But first I want to talk about why this organization exists because it seems that that context has got a little muddy over the years Cheyenne's downtown was built by the railroad It seen cattle barons on Millionaires Row Cheyenne Frontier Days that turned into long celebratory nights and had sustained itself from the mid 20th century excuse me from the mid- 20th century But by the late 1970s it was declining And like most American downtowns at that time with suburban sprawl shifting retail demand and the expansion of the interstate system they were all affecting thriving business districts at a devastating pace At its worst the Cheyenne downtown vacancy rate hit 40% In 1980 a group of Cheyenne residents formed a downtown development association to help But by 1984 it was clear that an entity with bigger muscle was needed Once legislation was was passed the downtown development authority a municipal board was created by the Cheyenne governing body with approval from the Cheyenne voters The measure itself passed by a margin of more than 2 to1 in what was at the time the largest voter turnout of any special citywide election in Cheyenne's history That same year the DDA applied and was selected to become one of the urban demonstration cities in the National Main Street Project Five years after the DDA was established downtown vacancy dropped from 40 to to 5% However from 1990 to present the DDA has had its challenges Many things have been done and many things have been left unresolved It's not for lack of planning We're very good at that As you can docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk March 17, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Absent: Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenn e Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, advised the parties remain at an impasse regarding wages and expressed a preference to proceed with reviewing other sections of the contract. Mayor Collins emphasized the City’s goal of maintaining Cheyenne Fire Rescue as the best place to work. He reviewed current staffing levels, new fire stations, apparatus and equipment, and highlighted the City’s ongoing investments in firefighter safety. Mayor Collins expressed concern about losing momentum on progress made in negotiations and further reviewed compensation data, stating that Cheyenne firefighters are currently the highest paid in the state. He provided additional comparative information f or Loveland, CO , including staffing levels, call volumes per station, number of stations, battalion chief assignments, as well as cost of living considerations and noted that Loveland is not unionized. He reiterated that wages remain the primary point of concern and expressed reluctance to move forward with other sections of the agreement at this time. Mr. Thoms requested a recess at 6:20 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the HR conference room to caucus. Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 6:45 p.m. Mr. Thoms acknowledged that wages remain the primary issue and expressed the Union’s desire to continue moving forward with negotiations. Mayor Collins stated that the parties remain at a standstill pending agreement on certain key issues. Mr. Thoms requested that previously referenced data be provided for review in advance of the next meeting. There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially adjourned at 6:49 p.m. Submitted by, Kylie Soden, City Clerk This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle March 20, 2026

17th 2026 meeting of the Finance Committee to order Ask if you're in the room that you silence your cell phones Uh making public comment clearly identify yourself when making public comment online Use the raised hand function in person approach the podium and please turn on the microphone and there will be no additional business discussed after the completion of this agenda All communications go through the chair and with that miss uh clerk give us the first item please Number 12 ordinance third reading repealing the ordinance number 463 which specified the monthly storm water runoff management system user fee in accordance with section 13.32.050 of the municipal code of the city of Cheyenne Wyoming Do we have a staff report Madam chief of staff chair through you Amber Ash chief of staff for the city of Cheyenne Um before you for consideration is the repeal of the storm water user fees on third and final reading Um this is pursuant to conversations with the legislature um an agreement that the administration would act in good faith um with the legislature to identify and work on alternative options to resolve our storm water runoff needs Any questions from the committee to the chief of staff Not seeing any We'll go to public comment Labour Welcome Uh thank you chairman I uh want to comment on this most unusual and I think ill advised action It is uh as I'm sure you're all aware we spent over a year a lot of money and really did quite a bit of outreach to communicate the dangers that we face from storm water runoff And while I recognize what happened at the legislature I wonder if that's adequate I wonder if this is really uh going to be the end here where there's an interim study of many water related issues This is certainly not the only water related issue in the select committee Um and certainly probably it's a probably some information come out of it But I want to emphasize uh Mr chairman the uh period of time that we're living in I want to emphasize that today about half of Nebraska is on fire The East Coast is being racked by tornadoes We just had a totally unprecedented uh do storm that caused damage to a lot of uh people and businesses and trees around here And yet um we can't seem to get it together to do much about storm water management And I would suggest to you uh members of the committee and to the public or any of the staff that it's really essential that we don't just wait and hope that the legislature is going to find a way to assist and they will have to assist all the municipalities in Wyoming with storm water management I don't think you can say Cheyenne is uh that important Certainly we know that the other communities that have these uh programs in place are going to continue They're relatively minor Laramie repealed theirs But I hope I'm making my point here Mr Chairman Uh summer's coming Uh we all know that the storms are much much worse But I would suggest that we should be looking at going to the absolute worst danger spots in our drainage

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk March 16, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Absent: Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, emphasized the Union’s priority of maintaining fair market wages and noted that peer departments, including those along the Front Range, provide relevant comparisons. Jason Lindsay, Vice President of Local #279, presented pension and salary comparisons for firefighters in Wyoming, Colorado, and Montana. Discussion included specialty pay, Cheyenne’s economic growth, and cost-of-living data sourced from bestplaces.net. Mr. Thoms presented a counter proposal which included updates to Section 19 – Inclement Weather and Section 21 – Classification of Employment and Basic Wages. Additional discussion included recruitment efforts, attrition history, firefighter candidate pools, appropriate peer comparisons, the importance of aligning recurring revenues with recurring expenses, as well as the City’s use of reserves. Pursuant to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr. Segrave moved to meet in executive session, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio and video recording of the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:41 p.m. in the City Council office] Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting at 7:06 p.m. and discussion continued regarding wage comparisons, specialty pay, and appropriate peer groups, including how comparable communities structure and fund compensation. Mayor Collins expressed the belief that the City’s firefighters are not underpaid. Discussion also included cost-of-living comparisons among certain Wyoming communities, paramedic compensation and training considerations, and ongoing challenges in reaching an agreement on wage comparisons and the identification of appropriate peer groups. The City reiterated its standing offer related to wage increases. The Union requested adjournme nt to review rank average amounts provided by the City. There being no further business to come before the governing body

Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe . Absent: Dr. Rinne. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn , Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session. Pursuant to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr. Segrave moved to meet in executive session, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio and video recording of the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:04 p.m. in the City Council office] Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting at 6:33 p.m. Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, expressed appreciation for the Governing Body’s support and positive relationship with the Union. He briefly reviewed the Union’s request, noting that no wage increase was requested last year and emphasiz ed the need to remain competitive within the regional market. Mayor Collins thanked the Union for its constructive relationship with the City and acknowledged their concerns. He noted the importance of identifying an appropriate peer group for compensation comparisons and provided an overview of benefits offered in Cheyenne compared to other Wyoming communities, including retirement , wages and specialty and longevity pay. Mayor Collins stated that, in many cases, Cheyenne’s compensation is more favorable and noted that working in other states can involve a higher cost of living due to factors including income and property taxes. He also provided a brief overview of the City’s proposal. Mr. Thoms requested a recess at 6:43 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the H R conference room to caucus. Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 7:11 p.m., at which time it was agreed to adjourn until the next meeting. There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially adjourned at 7:12 p.m. Submitted by, Kylie Soden, City Clerk This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle March 18, 2026

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk March 9, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Tom Segrave , Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #21 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Dr. Rinne moved to suspend the rules to change the order of the agenda to bring forward agenda item #22 (Resolution regarding support of the Professional Rodeo Cowboy Association) for action immediately prior to agenda item #7, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no.” [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 23, 2026. docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk March 5, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave (via Zoom), Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. Absent: Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons and Dr. Rinne . Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session. Pursuant to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr. Wolfe moved to meet in executive session, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk and Chief Andrew Dykshorn and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio and video recording of the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:05 p.m. in the Mayor’s conference room] Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting at 6:40 p.m. Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, expressed appreciation for the labor -management meetings that take place in advance of contract negotiation meetings. He stated the Union’s primary goal is to address firefighter wages and presented wage comparisons for firefighter positions in Wyoming, Colorado, Montana, and South Dakota. Mr. Thoms indicated it is the Union’s position that Cheyenne firefighter compensati on falls behind regional standards. Upon a request for clarification on the jurisdictions used for wag e comparisons , Mr. Thoms provided additional information and stated that Cheyenne competes with departments along the Front Range. Mayor Collins stated that Wyoming communities are the most appropriate peer comparisons and noted the City has not experienced significant recruitment or retention issues in recent years. Mr. Thoms indicated the Union’s analysis includes both starting and top -out wages and that Cheyenne falls behind some communities in top-out compensation. Discussion continued regarding differences in municipal funding structures, statewide compensation averages, top-out wages, identification of appropriate peer communities with similar tax structures and populations, and the number of applicants for entry-level firefighter positions. Submitted by, Kylie Soden, City Clerk This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle March 11, 2026

the meeting to order Welcome to the March 2nd public service committee We would ask the public and staff to turn cell phones off or to set them to vibrate and mute if their devices are online Um if you want to make a public comment online please use the raise hand function or um approach the podium if you're here with us in person and turn the microphone on You can just push the button We would specified private displays Okay And do we have a staff report okay up there Uh good afternoon Madam Chairwoman David Hopinson deputy city attorney Uh this proposed ordinance just again very briefly uh creates a new chapter 8.72 and provides some regulation and guidance on the private uh for private displays on public property be happy to answer any questions that any of you may have with respect to the ordinance or how it may work Okay Do we does the committee have any questions for the presenter all right Um and we'll go to public comment Is there any public comment on this okay That's all right Uh my name is Chelsea McCort Um and I am in Ward One Um I wanted to briefly touch on how in general this whole uh public display on private property feels a lot like a personal agenda that someone doesn't like how something looks that's being pushed through as a city level ordinance Um there's a number of different reasons Number one um I my background is in anthropology It is really bad for culture when we criticize how other people mourn and when we remove opportunities that allow them to mourn Um it's disrespectful to the people who have passed away It's disrespectful to the family and it truly does destroy culture Um there the issue that keeps being brought up that it's a safety concern is not actually true um studies 2019 2011 both show that uh the presence of memorials RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk February 23, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in special session on this date beginning at 5:30 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting, for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association of Firefighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave (via Zoom), Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe . Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk , Amber Ash, Chief of Staff, John Brodie, City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue . The pledge of allegiance was recited. Mayor Collins provided opening remarks and emphasized the importance of the labor -
management discussions that take place in advance of formal negotiations. The proposed Ground Rules were reviewed, agreed upon, and signed by both the City and the Union. [Clerk’s Note: The City’s spokespersons are Mayor Patrick Collins, City Attorney John Brodie, and Chief of Staff Amber Ash. The Union’s spokespersons are Union President Chris Thoms, Union Vice President Jason Lindsay, and Union Grievance Representative James Lewis.] Mayor Collins announced that additional negotiation meetings will be scheduled in the coming weeks to review City and Union proposals. There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially adjourned at 5:33 p.m. Submitted by, Kylie Soden, City Clerk This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle March 6, 2026

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk January 12, 2026 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), Tom Segrave, Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #22 (a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Esquibel moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 22, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Election of C ity Council President for 2026. Mayor Collins stated that, pursuant to City Code, the mayor conducts the election for Council President but does not cast a vote. Mr. Esquibel moved to nominate and elect Mr. Segrave as City Council President, seconded by Mr. White. Dr. Aldrich moved to cease nominations, seconded by Mr. W olfe. Motion to cease nominations carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Motion to elect Mr. Segrave as City Council President carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote. Election of City Council Vice-President for 2026 . docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee 01-06-26 1] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee 01-06-26 Context/Agenda: good afternoon welcome to the January 6 2026 Finance Committee meeting want to remind everyone to please turn off their cell phones or move them to vibrate or mute any devices they might bring when making public comment clearly identify yourself please to make public comment online use the raise hand function online in person point approach the podium and please turn on the microphone and adjust it to where you can uh speak clearly into it uh the public uh there is no additional business to be discussed following completion of this agenda clerk please read the first item number eight ordinance third reading defining the terms and conditions of employment for sworn officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for January 2026 until the end of fiscal year 2026 staff report all right Mr chairman members of the committee Captain David Jane Shy Police Department what you have before you is a repeal and replace ordinance of our terms and conditions the only substantive change in here is the 3% increase uh the cost of living adjustment uh which has already been funded and and approved through that and that's reflected on exhibit B within this uh contract and I stand for any questions any questions for the captain hearing none any public comment any public comment online no uh may I have a motion please um Mr chairman I move to approve on third and final reading moved by Moody mr chairman I second that motion second by Wolf uh any discussion from the committee hearing none all those in favor i I I the recommendation uh for the me for Monday's meeting will be to approve on third and final reading next item please number 16 resolution approving a sponsorship by Bison Beverage for Cheyenne Frontier Days events occurring July 17th through July 26th of 2026 July 23rd through August 1st 2027 and July 21st through July 30th of 2028 staff report mr chairman members of the committee Kylie Soden city clerk the item before you is a resolution that approves a three-year sponsorship between Bison Beverage and Cheyenne Frontier Days for 2026 2027 and 2028 approval of the licensing authority is required under Wyoming statute 12-5-42 which regulates transactions between alcohol industry representatives and retail liquor license holders tram Frontier Days qualifies for the statutory exception that allows this type of sponsorship as they are nonprofit taxexempt organization that has operated continuously for more than two years and I am available for any questions you may have any questions Mr escoel oh sorry questions is there a representative of uh Cheyenne Frontier Day is here to speak to tell us a little bit more about this tom Hig Cheyen Frontier Days um Mr chairman I think uh this is pretty self-explanatory it's been a relationship we've had for a long time with the Louiswis family and bison beverage um but uh we sure appreciate your support on on approving that sponsorship any questions thank you hearing none any public comment any public comment online hearing none may I have a motion mr chair I move to adopt second moved by Esabel second

docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Public Services Committee 01-05-26] Context/Agenda: # Public Services Committee 01-05-26 Context/Agenda: wow a lot of people here Mhm Good afternoon and welcome to the January 5th 2026 Public Services Committee Um I would ask that anyone in the room silence your phone or your electronics if you could please Uh we have one item on the agenda today That's the only thing we'll be considering No no walk-ons for the committee Um if you'd like to speak to the group we'll have a open discussion both online and uh in person With that uh Jennifer could we have a first item please number nine ordinance second reading creating chapter 1.28 28 administrative inspection warrants establishing authority for their issuance and amending the municipal code of the city of Cheyenne Wyoming to authorize certain city officials as specified to apply for administration administrative inspection warrants And could we have a staff report please good afternoon Chairman David Hopinson deputy city attorney Welcome Um I was just going to give kind of a brief overview about inspection warrants generally and I would defer kind of the policy to the uh the chief building official or uh the fire chief to speak to the uh the committee as far as the need for the ordinance But what this ordinance uh just briefly does is it allows or puts into code um and allows the chief fire uh or the chief of the fire department and the uh chief building official to seek administrative inspection warrants Uh and the kind of the purpose for that is to allow them when there's a need for the enforcement of municipal code or state law uh that's administrative in nature as opposed to criminal in nature it kind of creates the framework for that Uh really just brief history kind of prior to 1967 um uh code enforcement or code officials had a lot more leeway as far as being able to go on to properties for inspection purposes Uh the Supreme Court in that year uh held that you know you can't do that There's still got to be some framework even though the standard might be lower And so what they kind of ended up with are what we call administrative inspection warrants which have a lower standard of proof or or cause rather uh with respect to entering into a person's property uh primarily because the nature of uh the inspection is not criminal It's simply to enforce uh municipal code and ordinance it has lower requirements in that sense Uh as well as allowing them when it's reasonable legislative or administrative standards for conducting kind of routine inspections are in place or if they do have probable cause they could still get in uh or authorize a warrant under that standard or if the inspection is reasonably necessary to determine discover or verify the condition of a property Um so in that sense it's a little bit easier to get this kind of warrant but also the consequences for people are less than than you would see under a criminal standard I'm happy to speak more about that Happy to dive down into the details of the the ordinance as as the committee seeks but otherwise would stand for questions Thank you David Questions from the committee for staff Dr Thank you M
